S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S069.name: Intrusive_Symptoms
S069.description: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.

subtypes.Intrusive Memories: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Distressing Dreams: Recurrent distressing dreams in which the content and/or affect of the dream are related to the traumatic event.
subtypes.Dissociative Reactions (Flashbacks): Dissociative reactions (e.g., flashbacks) in which the individual feels or acts as if the traumatic event were recurring.
subtypes.Psychological Distress at Cues: Intense or prolonged psychological distress at exposure to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Physiological Reactions to Cues: Marked physiological reactions to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.

S070.name: Trauma_Avoidance
S070.description: Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event.

subtypes.Internal Avoidance: Efforts to avoid distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings about or closely associated with the traumatic event.
subtypes.External Avoidance: Efforts to avoid external reminders (people, places, conversations, activities, objects, situations) that arouse distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings.

S073.name: Distorted_Cognitions_With_Blame
S073.description: Persistent, distorted cognitions about the cause or consequences of the traumatic event that lead the individual to blame himself/herself or others.

subtypes.Self-Blame: Blaming oneself for the occurrence of the trauma or for not preventing it.
subtypes.Blaming Others: Distorting the situation to blame specific others for the occurrence or damage of the trauma.

S074.name: Persistent_Negative_Emotional_State
S074.description: Persistent negative emotional state (e.g., fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame).

subtypes.Persistent Fear: A state of constant fear, anxiety, and tension.
subtypes.Persistent Horror: The shock and terror of the traumatic moment do not fade and remain.
subtypes.Persistent Anger: A state of chronic anger boiling inside or being expressed aggressively.
subtypes.Persistent Guilt: Unceasing feelings of guilt or remorse related to the trauma.
subtypes.Persistent Shame: Continuing to feel shame or humiliation due to the trauma.

S075.name: Social_Detachment
S075.description: Feelings of detachment or estrangement from others.

subtypes.Emotional Detachment: Feeling cut off from others even when physically present, unable to feel connection.
subtypes.Social Isolation: Increasingly isolating oneself and not participating in social activities or gatherings.
subtypes.Difficulty with Intimacy: Distancing oneself from close people as it is difficult to become emotionally close.
subtypes.Loss of Belonging: Feeling like an outsider who belongs nowhere.

S077.name: Irritability_Aggression
S077.description: Irritable behavior and angry outbursts (with little or no provocation) typically expressed as verbal or physical aggression.

subtypes.Impulsive Anger: Sudden explosions of anger for trivial reasons or no clear reason.
subtypes.Verbal Aggression: Attacking others with shouting, cursing, or blame without holding back.
subtypes.Physical Aggression: Physically attacking people or throwing/breaking objects.
subtypes.Chronic Irritability: A state where nerves are always sharp and sensitive, ready to explode at the slightest touch.

S078.name: Reckless_Self_Destructive_Behavior
S078.description: Reckless or self-destructive behavior pattern that endangers one's safety or health.

subtypes.Risky Behaviors: Reckless actions disregarding consequences, such as speeding, dangerous sports, or criminal acts.
subtypes.Substance Abuse: Excessive drinking or drug use to harm oneself.
subtypes.Indisicriminate Sexual Behavior: Engaging in unprotected or dangerous sexual activities repetitively.
subtypes.Self-Harm: Actions that intentionally harm or scar one's own body.

S079.name: Hypervigilance
S079.description: Persistent state of being alert and tense about the surrounding environment.

subtypes.Scanning for Danger: Always scanning the surroundings and being alert to find potential threats or risks.
subtypes.Safety Checking: Repetitively confirming safety, such as checking exit locations or observing people around.
subtypes.Sustained Alertness: Unable to relax tension even in safe environments and maintaining a constant state of alertness.

patient_info.stressor_event: Death of a close family member
patient_info.stressor: Two years and three months ago, Lacedrick’s younger cousin, who had been active in his church youth program and pickup basketball circle, was fatally shot near the community center after an evening event Lacedrick had helped organize. Because he had been one of the first family members to reach the scene, the loss became bound up with repeated intrusive recollections, avoidance of the court and nearby blocks, and a persistent conviction that he had failed both his cousin and the young people he was called to protect. As the months stretched into years, his preaching, music, photography, and community work narrowed under guilt, anger, detachment, poor concentration, hypervigilance in the neighborhood, angry outbursts during ministry meetings, and reckless attempts to patrol or confront people he associated with danger. He came to psychiatric attention when the senior pastor placed him on temporary leave after a volatile church-board incident and arranged a clergy mental-health evaluation rather than treating it as a discipline problem alone.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.
S025.manifestation: I used to love preaching, playing keys, taking pictures, and running with the guys on the court, but now I mostly go through the motions or avoid it altogether because none of it feels alive in me anymore.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.
S031.manifestation: When I sit down to write a sermon or even answer church emails, my mind blanks out and I read the same line five or six times without taking in what it says.

S069.name: Intrusive_Symptoms
S069.description: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.
S069.manifestation: What brings me in is that I keep getting hit out of nowhere with the scene of my cousin on that pavement, like I can hear the shouting and see the lights again even when I'm standing in the church office trying to act normal.

S070.name: Trauma_Avoidance
S070.description: Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event.
S070.manifestation: I take the long way around town so I don't pass the community center or that court, and if somebody starts talking about that night I shut it down or find a reason to leave.

S073.name: Distorted_Cognitions_With_Blame
S073.description: Persistent, distorted cognitions about the cause or consequences of the traumatic event that lead the individual to blame himself/herself or others.
S073.manifestation: I keep telling myself that if I had ended the event earlier, walked him out, or kept better watch over those boys, my cousin would still be here.

S074.name: Persistent_Negative_Emotional_State
S074.description: Persistent negative emotional state (e.g., fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame).
S074.manifestation: Most days I feel this mix of fear, anger, and guilt sitting in my chest from the time I wake up, like I failed God, my family, and the kids who trusted me.

S075.name: Social_Detachment
S075.description: Feelings of detachment or estrangement from others.
S075.manifestation: Even when I'm surrounded by people at church calling me 'brother' and asking me to pray, I feel like I'm behind glass and nobody can really reach me.

S077.name: Irritability_Aggression
S077.description: Irritable behavior and angry outbursts (with little or no provocation) typically expressed as verbal or physical aggression.
S077.manifestation: I've snapped in ministry meetings over small things, raising my voice at deacons or youth leaders like they're the enemy, and afterward I hate how fast I went there.

S078.name: Reckless_Self_Destructive_Behavior
S078.description: Reckless or self-destructive behavior pattern that endangers one's safety or health.
S078.manifestation: Some nights I drive around the blocks near the center looking for the faces I think might be trouble, and I've gotten out of the car to confront people even though I know it could get me shot too.

S079.name: Hypervigilance
S079.description: Persistent state of being alert and tense about the surrounding environment.
S079.manifestation: I can't sit with my back to a door anymore, and at church events I'm always watching hands, corners, cars slowing down, and where the nearest exit is instead of paying attention to the people in front of me.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I was put on temporary leave from ministry after I blew up in a church-board meeting, and I’ve had to step back from leading youth events because people don’t trust me to stay steady right now.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on since my cousin was killed two years and three months ago.
